svg.title: Approach, rotation and push to clear access to a shelf target
svg.desc: Three snapshots of the same open-sided shelf. A five-finger robot hand approaches a blocker in front of an untouched target, rotates the blocker so that the selected OBB face's inward normal matches the commanded push direction, then changes from hooked-finger contact to a broad palm contact and pushes along that direction to open access. The commanded direction is drawn from the object center of mass, which is placed at the geometric center for this uniform-density illustration only. Four separate, jointed fingers and an opposed thumb are shown in schematic projection, with a blue wrist and silver arm. Finger links are not a validated RH56E2 kinematic model; the projection does not imply that all digits contact the object. Shelf pillars and other objects stay fixed. These drawings do not prescribe a particular contact configuration.
svg.text: Task top view · Five-finger hand in schematic projection

g.text: Curl the fingers around the rear-side edge
Use finger contact to turn the selected face toward d_push
Push with the palm to open access
Broaden contact while retaining face–direction alignment
CoM marks the arrow origin, not a rotation pivot.
The goal sets its direction; it is not a force arrow.
Same direction, not just parallel: e_align → 0.
Translate along d_push while retaining alignment.
Contact forces must also control unwanted rotation.

svg.text: Orange: selected OBB face / inward normal · Blue: desired translation · Teal: palm contact · Green: target access · Hook-to-palm motion is illustrative.
* CoM is drawn at the geometric center for this uniform-density box only. Exact CoM is not a policy input; general objects can have an offset CoM.
